question: How many Starlink satellites will be in orbit on September 3, 2026, per Jonathan McDowell's tracker?
resolution_criterion: This question resolves to the value shown in the "Total In Orbit" field on Jonathan McDowell's Starlink Statistics page (https://planet4589.org/space/con/star/stats.html) using the first page snapshot stamped on or after 00:00 UTC on September 3, 2026. For example, if the page shows "Total In Orbit: 11150", the question resolves as 11150. If no update is stamped between 00:00 UTC September 3 and the end of September 4, 2026, use the most recent snapshot available before then.
reference_class: 3-4 day-ahead changes in McDowell's Starlink 'Total In Orbit' during the 2026 Falcon-9-only cadence regime (net ~+6.5/day: 10876 on Jul 30 -> 11028 Aug 21 -> 11093 Aug 31), combined with his observed page-update gap distribution
dispersion_basis: SD of ~3-day changes in Total In Orbit in the 2026 Falcon-9-only regime ~9 sats (net +6.5/day with 27-sat launch lumpiness) x 2.56 = 23; the bimodal update-timing branch (11093 vs ~11112) spans about the same width
reasoning:
[pooled 3 independent research runs (angles P,P,P): medians 1.109e+04/1.11e+04/1.111e+04 -> 1.11e+04; the narrative below is the P-angle run's own view]
Live check of planet4589.org/space/con/star/stats.html at 2026-09-03 ~22:00Z shows the page still stamped 'Data last updated: 2026 Aug 31 2104:48' with Total In Orbit 11093 (launched 12881, working 11078). So no Sep 3 stamp existed 22h into Sep 3. Only one launch fell in the gap (Starlink 15-23, 27 sats, 0842 UTC Sep 2); the next is Sep 6, slipped from Sep 4/5. If McDowell posts an update stamped Sep 3 or Sep 4, it should read 11093 + 27 - ~5-8 reentries = 11110-11117. If he does not (he is already 3 days stale, and his stamps run ~21:00 UTC with multi-day gaps: Aug 21 19:59, Aug 31 21:04), the criterion's fallback gives 11093. The criterion is also genuinely ambiguous between 'first page snapshot stamped >= Sep 3' meaning the page's own data stamp (-> ~11112) and an archive capture taken on Sep 3 (Wayback captures ~11:43 UTC daily, which would show 11093); the scheduled resolution time of Sep 3 12:00Z also lands on 11093. I put ~55% on 11093 and ~43% on 11110-11117, hence a median pinned just above 11093 with the upper quartiles covering the launch-added branch. Both bounds are far away with no mechanism to reach them, so no escape mass.

question: Which quantum pure-play stock will post the highest weekly gain from Aug 28 to Sep 4, 2026: IonQ, Rigetti, D-Wave, or Quantum Computing Inc.?
resolution_criterion: This question resolves based on each stock's percentage price change from its regular-session closing price on Friday, August 28, 2026 to its regular-session closing price on Friday, September 4, 2026, using the daily "Close" values published on the historical price pages at StockAnalysis.com for each ticker: IonQ (https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/IONQ/history/), Rigetti (https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/RGTI/history/), D-Wave Quantum (https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/QBTS/history/), and Quantum Computing Inc. (https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/QUBT/history/). The percentage change for each ticker is (Sep 4 close − Aug 28 close) / Aug 28 close. The option corresponding to the ticker with the largest (most positive) percentage change resolves Yes; all others resolve No. For example, a stock going from a $20.00 close to a $23.00 close is a +15% change.
reference_class: Fri-to-Fri weekly top-gainer among the four US quantum pure-plays (IONQ/RGTI/QBTS/QUBT), conditioned on the state 4/5 days into the window; leadership rotates frequently and the higher-beta names (QUBT beta 3.79, RGTI, QBTS) win 'biggest gainer' weeks somewhat more often than the largest, lowest-beta name
reasoning:
[pooled 3 independent research runs (angles P,P,P): 'IonQ (IONQ)' 0.37/0.54/0.45 -> 0.46; the narrative below is the P-angle run's own view]
Four of five trading days in the Aug 28 -> Sep 4 window are already closed. Verified closes give week-to-date IONQ -0.46%, QBTS -1.00%, QUBT -2.33%, RGTI -2.63% (Aug 28 and Sep 3 closes confirmed on both the StockAnalysis history pages and the live quote pages; the Aug 26 rows also match the reported 'D-Wave sinks 8% on CFO retirement' session, so the series is coherent). Only Sep 4 remains. Cross-sectional residual dispersion after removing the daily sector mean was ~1.3pp/day over the last seven sessions (one 2.9pp day on the D-Wave CFO news, three sub-0.3pp days), implying ~1.5-2.6pp per-name idiosyncratic SD; an argmax integral over four normals with those gaps and sigma=2.6pp gives roughly IONQ 0.40 / QBTS 0.31 / QUBT 0.15 / RGTI 0.13. I shaved ~3pp off IonQ toward the high-betas because these names are beta-ordered, not symmetric: on large risk-on days (May 21: QBTS +25%, RGTI +24%, QUBT +14% vs IONQ +10%) the smaller names dominate, and Friday Sep 4 carries the August payrolls print. D-Wave's Leap gate-model simulator is slated for 'September 2026' with no announced date - a live but unscheduled QBTS catalyst that only needs a small pop to close a 0.54pp gap. No prediction market covers this contract. Main uncertainty is that Aug 28 anchors are single-sourced and the IONQ-QBTS gap is inside plausible data noise.
what_would_change_my_mind: A dated D-Wave press release (Leap gate-model simulator GA, contract win) landing pre-market or intraday Sep 4
A strong risk-on payrolls session on Sep 4 (sector up >4%), which historically hands leadership to QUBT/RGTI/QBTS over IONQ
Any correction to the Aug 28 closes, since the IONQ-QBTS gap is only 0.54pp
Overnight single-name news on RGTI (CHIPS letter-of-intent) or QUBT worth >3%
